name: Sri Muthumariamman Temple, Matale
deity: Muthumariamman (Mariamman, goddess of rain and fertility)
significance: The main Hindu temple of the Sri Lankan hill town of Matale, raised on paddy land gifted in 1852 and completed in 1874 under Nattukottai Chettiar patronage. Its 108-foot rajagopuram, finished in 2007 and carrying over a thousand sculpted figures, is one of the tallest temple towers on the island.

name: Shiva Mandir, Johi
significance: A mid-19th-century Shiva temple in the Sindhi town of Johi, known locally as the Qubi for its unusual pair of domes and its mix of iron, cement and cheeroli construction. The idols once fixed to its outer walls were destroyed after Partition, and only their traces survive.

name: Kokkadicholai Thaanthonreeswarar Temple
significance: A Shaiva temple southwest of Batticaloa, ascribed to Ulaga Naachi of the Chola realm and counted among the oldest and most important Shiva kovils in Sri Lanka. Its lingam is reported to be a naturally formed one, a rarity on the island.
story: Local tradition holds that the temple's stone bull came to life, grazed on the grass and drove Portuguese soldiers away from the shrine.

name: Magderu Temple, Dhrasanvel
significance: An 8th-century saptayatana temple near Dwarka, its large central shrine ringed by six smaller ones, now a Monument of National Importance in the ASI's Vadodara Circle. Scholars link the name element Maga to the Aboti Maga Brahmins, Surya worshippers who migrated from Iran to western India, and read the site as an original sun temple.

name: Raghunath Temple, Srinagar
significance: A Dogra-period Rama temple in Srinagar, begun in 1835 under Maharaja Gulab Singh and completed in 1860 under Maharaja Ranbir Singh. Attacked and left abandoned after the exodus of Kashmiri Hindus, it is now undergoing restoration.

name: Gobindram Darbar, Manjhand
style: Brick Hindu temple with arched entrances, carved brickwork and frescoes
significance: A Shiva temple, known locally simply as the Shiva Temple, in the Indus-side town of Manjhand, founded by Gobindram and built of burnt brick bound with gypsum cheeroli paste. Until Partition it drew annual fairs of Hindu pilgrims from across Sindh, with a dharamshala alongside and performances by the Sindhi devotional singer Bhagat Kanwar Ram.

name: Shri Krishna Mandir, Islamabad
builtDisplay: land allotted 2016; ground broken 2020, construction pending
significance: The first Hindu temple granted permission to be built in Islamabad, on land allotted to the Pakistan Hindu Panchayat in 2016, with a groundbreaking in June 2020 and a government grant approved days afterwards. Construction had still not started as of 2025; the site was attacked and vandalised four times and its boundary wall pulled down in 2020.

name: Sri Sri Bura Shivdham
significance: A Shiva temple, also called Shivbari, standing north of the Central Shaheed Minar in Dhaka and founded during Jahangir's reign; a severe storm wrecked it in 1912 and Raja Bijay Chand Mahtab of Burdwan had it rebuilt. Its caretaker and several resident ascetics were killed by the Pakistani army in the 1971 liberation war, and the surrounding locality of Shibbari takes its name from the temple.

name: Swarved Mahamandir
deity: Swarveda — 3,137 verses of the Vihangam Yoga scripture enshrined on its walls
style: Makrana marble and pink sandstone under a 125-petal lotus dome
significance: A seven-storey meditation temple at Varanasi, inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in December 2023 at a cost of around Rs 100 crore. Covering some 300,000 square feet and seating about 20,000 people, it carries 3,137 verses of the Swarveda across its walls.

name: Prasat Sa Kamphaeng Yai
place: Ban Sa Kamphaeng Yai, Uthumphon Phisai district
deity: Shiva (the sanctuary later passed to Mahayana Buddhist use)
significance: An 11th-century Khmer sanctuary in Sisaket province, raised under Udayadityavarman II as a Shiva temple and later converted to Mahayana Buddhist use. Restoration by Thailand's Fine Arts Department recovered a 126 cm Baphuon-style bronze guardian, rated among the finest Khmer bronzes found and now in the National Museum in Bangkok.
